candidate_relations.reason: CVID, HIV with CD4 140/µL, and chronic prednisone explain susceptibility but do not identify the resistant CMV infection.
Despite cough and dyspnea, chest CT shows bronchiectasis without consolidation or ground-glass opacity, while serial CMV DNA rises.
No mass, lymphadenopathy, or tissue evidence of lymphoma is supplied; the decisive findings are CMV viremia and antiviral-resistance mutations.
Repeated CMV viral loads establish infection, but this label omits the UL97 and UL54 mutations defining treatment resistance.
A history of recurrent HSV does not explain the measured CMV DNA or CMV-specific UL97 and UL54 resistance variants, and CT lacks pneumonitis.
Previous MAC pulmonary infection is part of the immunocompromised history, whereas the current microbiologic trajectory is persistent CMV viremia.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis and absence of ground-glass opacities make Pneumocystis an unsupported explanation for this resistant viremia.
The C592G UL97 and N408K UL54 variants demonstrate antiviral resistance, but this phrase alone does not name CMV or the active infection.
No pulmonary infiltrates or retinitis are present, so specifying CMV pneumonitis or disseminated disease extends beyond the documented resistant infection and viremia.
Chronic bronchiectasis and past MAC lung disease are documented, but they do not account for escalating CMV DNA during antiviral therapy.
UL97 C592G supports ganciclovir resistance, yet the additional polymerase mutation and multidrug reference scope are not fully conveyed.
This label captures CMV plus treatment resistance but does not state the multidrug phenotype reflected by concurrent UL97 and UL54 mutations.
The record provides neither current mycobacterial cultures nor systemic MAC lesions, while serial testing directly detects CMV.
MAC is a prior opportunistic infection in this patient and is not the infection linked to the current viral resistance genotype.
There is no temporal immune recovery or rising CD4 count; the CD4 remains 140/µL with virologically suppressed HIV.
Serial plasma CMV levels up to 3,171 IU/mL document viremia, but viremia alone omits the multidrug-resistant genotype.
Recurrent HSV belongs to the past history, whereas the active resistance mutations are in CMV UL97 and UL54 genes.
CT shows no nodules, cavitation, or consolidation attributable to aspergillosis and instead records only baseline bronchiectasis.
CMV disease identifies the pathogen-related illness but loses the central evidence of persistent viral load under therapy and dual resistance mutations.
The label includes active CMV infection and the multidrug resistance supported by persistent viremia plus UL97 C592G and UL54 N408K mutations.
